words.note: Pasangan: 打算怎么做. Hindari: 打算 is not a final decision; use 决定 once it is set. Example pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 打算 like the word you’ll use when someone asks your next workplace step and the plan can still change — e.g. talking with them tomorrow.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 打算 for a plan that is not locked yet. Switch to 决定 when the choice is already made.

example.pinyin: Wǒ dǎsuàn míngtiān hé tāmen tán.
example.en: I plan to talk with them tomorrow.

words.note: Pasangan: 做决定. Hindari: do not use 决定 for an idea that is still only under consideration. Example pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 决定 like the word you’ll use when a workplace option is already chosen — or when you say you still have not chosen which plan.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 决定 for a settled choice (or the act of settling it). If you are only weighing options, prefer 考虑.

example.zh: 我们还没决定用哪个方案。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen hái méi juédìng yòng nǎge fāng'àn.
example.en: We still haven’t decided which plan to use.

words.note: Pasangan: 考虑一下. Hindari: 我考虑一下 is not agreement; if there is a reply deadline, say when you will answer. Example pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 考虑 like the professional pause you’ll use when a workplace suggestion needs assessment before you answer.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 考虑一下 to buy time to evaluate. It does not mean yes; name a time if the other person needs a deadline.

example.zh: 这个建议不错，我再考虑一下。
example.pinyin: Zhège jiànyì búcuò, wǒ zài kǎolǜ yíxià.
example.en: This suggestion is good; I’ll consider it a bit more.

words.note: Pasangan: 想试一下. Hindari: 想 can mean “want” or “think”; what follows decides the sense. Example pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 想 like the natural word you’ll use for a simple workplace intention — wanting to hear someone’s idea first — more natural than 想要 in talk.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 想 + verb for everyday intentions at work. Context after 想 tells you whether it is “want to” or “think.”

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xiān tīngting nǐ de xiǎngfǎ.
example.en: I’d like to hear your thoughts first.

words.note: Pasangan: 需要帮助. Hindari: 需要 is stronger than 想; don’t use it for a light preference. Example pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 需要 like the word you’ll use when coworkers must supply something real — today’s data so you can report tomorrow.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 需要 for a real requirement, not a soft wish. Prefer 想 for a light preference.

example.zh: 我需要今天的数据，明天才能汇报。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào jīntiān de shùjù, míngtiān cái néng huìbào.
example.en: I need today’s data so I can report tomorrow.

words.note: Book prints pinyin as yào bù; standard conversational spelling is yàobù. Pasangan: 要不我们……. Hindari: 要不 usually offers an alternative — don’t stop right after the phrase. Example pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 要不 like the casual opener you’ll use when a workplace plan is stuck and you float another option — discuss again tomorrow.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers open an alternative with 要不我们…… and then finish the suggestion. Leaving only 要不 sounds incomplete.

example.en: How about we discuss it again tomorrow?

words.en: it would be better to; why not
words.note: Pasangan: 不如先……. Hindari: in a proposal, 不如 is not merely “not like”; it means the next option is better. Example pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 不如 like the word you’ll use when time is short at work and you recommend doing the most important part first.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 不如 to steer the group toward a better option than the one under discussion.

example.zh: 时间不多，不如我们先做最重要的部分。
example.pinyin: Shíjiān bù duō, bùrú wǒmen xiān zuò zuì zhòngyào de bùfen.
example.en: There’s not much time; we’d better do the most important part first.

words.en: it depends; see how things go
words.note: Pasangan: 到时候看情况. Hindari: don’t use 看情况 as an empty answer when you could already decide. Example pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 看情况 like the honest workplace answer when going tomorrow (or any plan) still depends on conditions that aren’t fixed.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 看情况 when the outcome is genuinely conditional. Name the condition if the other person needs to plan.

example.zh: 明天能不能去，要看情况。
example.pinyin: Míngtiān néng bu néng qù, yào kàn qíngkuàng.
example.en: Whether I can go tomorrow depends on the situation.

words.note: Pasangan: 我建议先……. Hindari: 建议 needs the content of the proposal — follow with a concrete action. Example pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 我建议 like the clear phrase you’ll use to offer a workplace next step without claiming the final call is yours — e.g. confirm time with the client first.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers follow 我建议 with a specific action. Stopping at 建议 alone is incomplete.

example.zh: 我建议先和客户确认时间。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jiànyì xiān hé kèhù quèrèn shíjiān.
example.en: I suggest we confirm the time with the client first.

words.note: Pasangan: 暂时不变. Hindari: 暂时 does not mean forever; say when it will be reviewed if relevant. Example pinyin not printed; standard pinyin added.
words.when: Remember 暂时 like the word you’ll use when a workplace arrangement stays as-is for now but can still change later.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 暂时 to limit a decision or state to the current period. Pair it with a review time when plans may shift.

example.en: This arrangement will not change for the time being.

notes.title: Module aim — state plans without overclaiming
notes.body: Modul 04 / Harian (book pages 15–17): state plans, options, and recommendations without sounding too certain before it is time. Indonesian title in the book: Niat dan keputusan.

notes.title: 打算 vs 决定
notes.body: From the book’s Hindari notes: 打算 marks a plan that can still change; use 决定 only when the choice is already set. Do not call something 决定 if it is still just under consideration.

example.pinyin: Wǒ dǎsuàn míngtiān hé tāmen tán.
example.en: I plan to talk with them tomorrow.

notes.title: 我考虑一下 is not yes
notes.body: The book warns that 我考虑一下 is not agreement. If there is a response deadline at work, say when you will answer.

example.zh: 这个建议不错，我再考虑一下。
example.pinyin: Zhège jiànyì búcuò, wǒ zài kǎolǜ yíxià.
example.en: This suggestion is good; I’ll consider it a bit more.

notes.title: Latihan 90 detik
notes.body: Book drill (p.17): pick three entries from this module — 打算, 需要, and 我建议. Make one work or daily story with all three. Record without reading, then check whether your timing and decisions are clear.
